Why exteriors go off

Melbourne is hard on the outside of a building

Nothing out there stays the colour it was laid. Damp shade, leaf litter, traffic film and metal staining all work on a surface at once, and most of it is reversible if it is dealt with before it sets into the material.

  1. Shade holds moisture, moisture grows

    South facing walls, covered alfresco areas and anything under a tree stay damp for most of winter. That is where the black spotting and the green film come from. It is biological, it spreads, and washing it off is not the same as killing it.

  2. Concrete is porous, so stains go in

    Exposed aggregate and broom finished concrete are full of open pores. Engine oil, tyre marks, barbecue fat and leaf tannin all soak down into them. Surface washing lightens the mark. Lifting it out takes the right chemistry and the right pressure.

  3. Gum and plane trees drop all year

    Melbourne's street trees do not shed neatly in autumn and stop. Leaf and bark build up in gutters and valleys continuously, and the tannin that washes out of them stains the paving underneath on the way down.

  4. Glass does not just get dirty, it etches

    Construction dust, sprinkler overspray and mineral run off from render leave deposits that bond to glass. Left long enough they mark the surface permanently. This is the main reason new build glazing needs cleaning before handover, not after.

How the work is done

Clean. Restore. Protect.

Whatever brought you here, the work itself runs in three stages. Most people call about the first one. The value is usually in the second and third, because a surface that has been restored and sealed stays clean for years rather than months.

  1. 01

    Clean

    Get the build up off. The right pressure and the right chemistry for the material, whether that is a concrete driveway or a rendered wall that cannot take pressure at all.

    • Pressure and surface cleaning
    • House and building washing
    • Soft washing for render and cladding
    • Windows, gutters, roof and solar
    • Builders and handover cleans
  2. 02

    Restore

    Deal with what washing does not shift. Stains that have gone into the material need treating rather than blasting, and blasting harder is how surfaces get damaged.

    • Rust and oil stain removal
    • Graffiti, paint and overspray
    • Efflorescence and mineral staining
    • Hard water and calcium marks
    • Mortar and cement residue
  3. 03

    Protect

    Seal the surface so the next clean is years away instead of months. This is the stage most exterior cleaners skip, and it is what separates a once a year job from a surface that keeps its finish.

    • Concrete and driveway sealing
    • Paver sealing and re-sanding
    • Exposed aggregate and stone sealing
    • Anti slip and anti graffiti coatings
    • Protective surface coatings

The same surface, one visit apart.
